correctness.rationale: The exact normalized Laguerre step inner products yield R_n(t)=exp(-t)-exp(-2t)B_n(t); Stieltjes derivative measure, Bochner integration and the triangle inequality prove reduction of the full real BV operator norm to single steps. The polynomial identity R_n' = exp(-t)(2exp(-t)Q_n-1) is independently checked. In CHECK.py all 2n distinct positive roots of Q_n'-Q_n (for each 1<=n<=5) are enclosed by rational sign changes, which exhaust degree 2n. Rigorous rational exponential Taylor bounds establish the signs of H_n-1/2 at those roots, thereby exhaust all candidate stationary locations, then rigorously enclose all residual heights. The exact lower bound for the third stationary location exceeds the upper bound for the first at n=5. For n=0..4 the first wins strictly. Uniqueness of the maximizing step and Hilbert-space equality identify all extremizers. Checker replay succeeded; numerical quadrature agrees but is not the proof. Limits: n>=6 and generalized weights unproved.

value.rationale: Exact sharp BV-to-L2 truncation norms for a canonical exponential Laguerre orthogonal system provide meaningful worst-case polynomial-chaos approximation benchmarks for discontinuous inputs. The first jump-optimizer relocation occurs at the natural first degree with an interior competitor overtaking the hard-edge branch; degrees 3,4 develop secondary stationary maxima without overtaking, creating a nontrivial structural threshold at degree 5. Its small but strictly positive winner gap requires global rational certification and could not be justified from isolated numerical root optimization. The result is an exact finite natural cutoff classification, with an explicitly stated higher-degree boundary, not an arbitrary slice or coefficient renaming.
